app.name: IND
app.one_liner: A cross-platform terminal coding agent that saves tokens, chunks work, shows usage, and remembers the project.
app.audience: Individual developers and small engineering teams using terminal-based AI coding tools.
app.platform: Cross-platform terminal CLI for Windows, macOS, and Linux
app.pricing: Free and local-first for MVP; future open-core or hosted team features are out of scope.
app.idea_verbatim: I want to build my own terminal coding tool like PI, named IND, with less AI token usage, chunked tasks, usage monitoring in the terminal, and memory. It should work on all devices and support local and all providers.
app.stack_preference: No fixed stack; choose a portable TypeScript and Node.js CLI architecture.
app.scope: IND MVP: a provider-neutral, token-efficient, chunked terminal coding agent with live usage telemetry and project memory.

validation.guardrail: Within 30 days of public testing, produce 10 benchmark runs across at least three environments and demonstrate median input-token reduction of at least 20 percent without reducing verified task completion.
risks: Existing agents already provide compaction and broad provider support.
Provider capability differences can make tools unreliable under one abstraction.
Token savings can be overstated unless compared with a fixed baseline.
Cross-platform terminal behavior requires Windows, macOS, and Linux verification.

economics.variable_cost: None when users bring keys or run local models

moves.move: Run a fixed 10-task benchmark against a full-context baseline
Observe five developers using terminal coding agents
Publish results across one local and two hosted providers

problem.statement: Terminal coding agents often send irrelevant repository context, repeat history, hide token and cost usage, execute oversized loops, and lose project decisions between sessions.
problem.proof: Pi documents compaction and context thresholds; Aider documents repository mapping; OpenCode documents broad provider support. These validate the category while leaving room for a transparent efficiency layer.
problem.workaround: Developers manually choose files, paste summaries, interrupt agents, inspect provider dashboards, and keep separate notes.
problem.jtbd: When I ask an AI coding agent to change my project, I want it to use only the context needed, work in safe chunks, show what it costs, and remember enough for the next session.

personas.name: The Cost-Conscious Builder
personas.who: A solo developer using hosted APIs for daily coding tasks.
personas.pain: Repeated context and hidden usage make experiments expensive.
personas.success: Completes the same verified tasks with a visible, lower token ledger.

personas.name: The Local-First Developer
personas.who: A developer running Ollama or another OpenAI-compatible local endpoint.
personas.pain: Provider tooling assumes cloud services and inconsistent capabilities.
personas.success: Uses local models with the same task, memory, and terminal workflow.

personas.name: The Terminal Team
personas.who: A small team that wants repeatable agent sessions without a hosted control plane.
personas.pain: Decisions and task state disappear between sessions.
personas.success: Reloads portable project memory and sees an auditable task history.

must: Start an IND session in any supported terminal and detect the project root.
Inspect the repository and build a relevance-ranked context set instead of sending the whole tree.
Plan a request into bounded task chunks with a visible checkpoint before each execution chunk.
Execute file edits and verification commands through a safe tool loop with approval settings.
Support a common provider adapter contract for OpenAI-compatible endpoints plus native adapters for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.
Apply context compression, output truncation, prompt caching where available, and configurable token budgets.
Show live input tokens, output tokens, estimated cost, latency, provider, model, savings, and chunk status in the terminal.
Persist project memory as Markdown and structured session usage as SQLite, then reload it on the next session.
Provide a deterministic benchmark command comparing IND context usage to a full-context baseline.
should: Allow model routing by task type, using a cheap model for summaries and a stronger model for difficult edits.
Support Ollama discovery and an explicit custom OpenAI-compatible base URL.
Offer commands to inspect, edit, export, and reset project memory.
Provide JSONL session events for external dashboards without making a dashboard part of the MVP.
wont: Hosted accounts, billing, team collaboration, or remote memory sync.
Unattended destructive commands or autonomous operation without safety controls.
Every provider-specific feature on the first release.

flows: User runs ind in a repository, selects or enters a task, reviews the generated plan and context budget, approves a chunk, watches the agent edit files and run verification, then continues or revises the next chunk.
User starts a session with a configured local or hosted provider, sees the provider/model and live usage bar, switches model or budget, and completes the task without changing the core workflow.
User exits and later runs ind resume; IND loads project memory, recent task state, changed files, and usage history, then proposes the next safe chunk.

auth: No IND account auth in MVP; provider credentials stay in environment variables or an OS-appropriate local credential store.
The CLI must never print secret values, write them to project memory, or send them to a model.
File and command permissions are controlled locally by the user and explicit approval settings.

kpis.metric: Median input-token reduction, verified task completion, chunk success rate, session resume success, and usage-ledger completeness.
kpis.tools: Local benchmark JSONL, SQLite usage ledger, and reproducible fixture repositories.
kpis.guardrail: At least 20 percent median input-token reduction with no more than 10 percent regression in verified benchmark completion.

risks: A common adapter contract may not expose equivalent tool calling, streaming, reasoning, or usage fields across providers.
Repository indexing can itself consume time and tokens if implemented as a full scan on every turn.
Estimated cost for local models is not monetary and must be labeled separately from cloud cost.
Command execution is security-sensitive and needs explicit allow, deny, and approval behavior.
decisions: Interpret all devices as cross-platform desktop terminals rather than native mobile apps.
Use a capability-based adapter interface: common chat, streaming, tool call, usage, and cancellation capabilities with graceful fallbacks.
Use SQLite for metrics and Markdown for portable memory so users can inspect and version the important state.
Keep the first release free and bring-your-own-key; defer hosted sync and billing.

features.value: Selects the smallest relevant file and symbol set for a task.
features.model: cheap local or fast hosted model with deterministic heuristics first
features.cost_rail: Hard input and output caps; prefer indexed metadata and cached summaries over raw file contents.
features.evals: 10 fixture tasks with expected relevant files and token ceilings.

features.value: Turns a request into bounded, reviewable coding chunks and produces edits plus verification steps.
features.model: cheap model for plan normalization; stronger configured model for hard edits
features.cost_rail: Per-chunk budget, maximum tool turns, timeout, cancellation, and model routing policy.
features.evals: Golden repository tasks covering add, modify, refactor, test, and bug-fix flows.

features.value: Compresses completed work and decisions into portable project memory.
features.model: cheap model with a strict schema and deterministic fallback
features.cost_rail: Summarize only changed files and unresolved decisions; never resummarize unchanged memory.
features.evals: Continuation tests where a new session must recover decisions and next steps.

ai.non_ai_fallback: Use deterministic file relevance rules, Git diff metadata, task chunk templates, and explicit user selection when a model is unavailable or exceeds budget.
ai.kill_guardrail: If context selection does not reduce median input tokens by 20 percent or memory continuation fails in 4 of 5 tests, redesign those subsystems before broadening provider support.

design.notes: Dark terminal-first interface with teal accent, semantic green/yellow/red states, compact status bar, explicit token ledger, no decorative panels. Must remain usable without color.

stack.framework: Node.js 20+ CLI with TypeScript and a thin command dispatcher
stack.ui: Ink-based terminal UI with ANSI-safe fallback output
stack.data: SQLite via better-sqlite3 or a portable equivalent plus Markdown memory files
stack.auth: No account auth in MVP; environment variables and local credential storage
stack.hosting: npm package and platform-specific release artifacts
stack.analytics: Local SQLite usage ledger and opt-in JSONL export; no remote analytics by default
stack.notes: Use provider adapters, capability detection, AbortController cancellation, zod schemas, Vitest, and fixture repositories. Keep the core independent from any single provider SDK.

workflows.title: Task to verified chunk
steps: Read project memory and Git status.
Parse the task and generate a bounded plan.
Rank relevant files and calculate the context budget.
Show the first chunk, expected edits, commands, and estimated usage.
Wait for approval according to the configured approval mode.
Stream the model response and execute only allowed tools.
Show the diff and run verification commands.
Record usage and outcome, update memory, and propose the next chunk.

workflows.title: Provider selection
steps: Read provider configuration.
Detect native and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Probe capabilities without sending project content.
Select a model using explicit configuration or task routing.
Fallback to deterministic behavior when the provider is unavailable.

workflows.title: Resume session
steps: Locate the project root and session database.
Load the latest memory and incomplete chunk.
Show changed files and unresolved decisions.
Recalculate a small context set rather than replaying the full transcript.
Ask for approval before continuing execution.

system_workflows.title: Context efficiency
steps: Use Git status and file metadata before reading content.
Use an indexed repository map and cached summaries.
Select only relevant files and symbols.
Truncate command output and deduplicate repeated observations.
Compact older session state at a configurable threshold.
Record baseline and actual input tokens for every model call.

system_workflows.title: Usage ledger
steps: Receive usage events from every adapter call.
Normalize token fields and mark estimates when unavailable.
Calculate cloud cost from configured price metadata.
Separate local compute metrics from monetary cost.
Render live totals in the terminal and persist SQLite rows.

system_workflows.title: Memory update
steps: Collect changed files, decisions, failures, and next steps.
Generate a schema-validated summary when a model is available.
Use a deterministic template fallback when it is not.
Append portable Markdown and upsert structured entries.
Load only relevant memory sections in future sessions.
